critique.evidence: The screen strongly supports Mastercard-relevant operating concerns with PR-AUC, recall under 0.1%/1% false-positive caps, calibration, alert load, p99 latency, confusion counts, fraud value caught, and good value blocked. The semantic/provenance ablation also connects evaluation to the intent-integrity architecture. However, it does not establish the dataset, sample period, class prevalence, monetary denominator, confidence intervals, or comparison with a conventional fraud baseline. All ablations show 100% fresh-row D recall, while removing semantics barely changes PR-AUC, so the distinctive intent-integrity contribution is not convincingly demonstrated. Successful real-server responses prove delivery, not metric validity.
critique.fix: Add a compact methodology and baseline panel: evaluation population and date range, attack/intent categories, monetary totals, confidence intervals, threshold used at each FPR cap, and comparison against rules or a standard fraud model. Include attack-family recall and value-weighted false-positive evidence, then explain why semantic and provenance layers materially improve unseen-intent detection.
